questions.stem: The maximum range of a projectile occurs at an angle of ……
questions.explanation: For projectile motion on level ground, the range $R = \frac{u^{2}\sin2\theta}{g}$. The range is maximum when $\sin2\theta = 1$, which occurs at $2\theta = 90^{\circ}$, hence $\theta = 45^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: A car travelling with a uniform velocity of $30\text{ ms}^{-1}$ along a horizontal road overcomes a constant frictional force of $600\text{ N}$. Calculate the power of the engine of the car.
questions.explanation: Power $P = Fv$. Substituting $F = 600\text{ N}$ and $v = 30\text{ ms}^{-1}$, $P = 600 \times 30 = 18000\text{ W}$.

questions.stem: Name the device that converts heat energy to electrical energy.
questions.explanation: A thermocouple converts heat energy directly into electrical energy using the Seebeck effect.

questions.stem: The point where the line of best fit cuts the vertical axis is called ………………………..
questions.explanation: The point where a graph cuts the vertical axis is known as the $y$-intercept.

questions.stem: Given $T^{2} = 4\pi^{2}\frac{l}{g}$, what is the correct equation for the value of $g$ if a graph of $T^{2}$ is plotted against $L$?
questions.explanation: From $T^{2} = \frac{4\pi^{2}}{g}L$, the slope $S = \frac{4\pi^{2}}{g}$. Rearranging gives $g = \frac{4\pi^{2}}{S}$.

questions.stem: A body moving at a constant speed accelerates when it is in
questions.explanation: In circular motion, the speed may be constant but the direction of velocity changes continuously, producing centripetal acceleration.

questions.stem: A body accelerates uniformly from rest at $2\text{ ms}^{-2}$. Calculate the magnitude of its velocity after travelling $4\text{ m}$.
questions.explanation: Using $v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$, with $u = 0, a = 2\text{ ms}^{-2}, s = 4\text{ m}$: $v^{2} = 2 \times 2 \times 4 = 16$, so $v = 4\text{ ms}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: An external force of magnitude $100\text{ N}$ acts on a particle of mass $0.15\text{ kg}$ for $0.03\text{ s}$. Calculate the change in the speed of the particle.
questions.explanation: Impulse equals change in momentum: $Ft = m\Delta v$. Hence $\Delta v = \frac{Ft}{m} = \frac{100 \times 0.03}{0.15} = 20\text{ ms}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: An object is said to undergo oscillatory motion when it moves.

options.B: To and fro about a fixed point

questions.explanation: Oscillatory motion is characterized by repeated to-and-fro motion about a mean or equilibrium position.

questions.stem: A body is rotating in a horizontal circle of radius $2.5\text{ m}$ with an angular speed of $5\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. Calculate the magnitude of the radial acceleration of the body.
questions.explanation: Radial acceleration $a = r\omega^{2}$. Substituting $r = 2.5\text{ m}$ and $\omega = 5\text{ rad s}^{-1}$, $a = 2.5 \times 25 = 62.5\text{ ms}^{-2}$.

questions.stem: If two vectors are represented thus: $\vec{A} = 5i + 2j + k$ and $\vec{B} = 2i + 4j - 3k$. Find $\vec{A} \times \vec{B}$.
questions.explanation: Cross product $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \det\begin{pmatrix} i & j & k \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 4 & -3 \end{pmatrix} = i(-6-4) - j(-15-2) + k(20-4) = -10i + 17j + 16k$.

questions.stem: The potential energy in an elastic string of force constant $K$ which has been extended by $x$ metres is expressed as?
questions.explanation: Elastic potential energy stored in a stretched spring or string: $PE = \frac{1}{2} K x^2$.

questions.stem: Time is a measure of?

options.C: Rate of change of physical events

questions.explanation: Time defines the duration or interval between the start and end of events.

questions.stem: The motion of a simple pendulum is represented thus; $a = -100 x$. What is the period of oscillation?
questions.explanation: For SHM: $a = -\omega^2 x$. Here $\omega^2 = 100$, so $\omega = 10\text{ rad/s}$. Period $T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \frac{2\pi}{10} = \frac{\pi}{5}\text{ s}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a unit of energy?
questions.explanation: Energy is measured in Joules, calories, or kilowatt-hours. Watt is a unit of power.

questions.stem: The displacement of a particle along the $X$-axis is given as $X = 5t^2 + 2$, where $X$ is in metres and $t$ in seconds. Calculate its instantaneous velocity at $t = 2\text{ s}$.
questions.explanation: Velocity $v = \frac{dX}{dt} = \frac{d(5t^2+2)}{dt} = 10t$. At $t=2\text{ s}$, $v = 10(2) = 20\text{ ms}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: The unit cycle per second is also called?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of frequency, cycles per second, is called Hertz (Hz).

questions.stem: The trajectory path of a projectile is?
questions.explanation: Under uniform gravity and neglecting air resistance, a projectile follows a parabolic path.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a fundamental unit?
questions.explanation: Fundamental SI units include meter, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, and candela. Others are derived.

questions.stem: The period of oscillation of a simple pendulum is related to its length $L$ and acceleration $g$ by $T = K L^x g^y$. Calculate the value of $x$ and $y$.
questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis: $[T] = [L]^x [LT^{-2}]^y$. This gives $x+y=0$ and $-2y=1$. Solving gives $y = -1/2$ and $x = 1/2$.

questions.stem: The position of an object on a velocity-time graph is given as $(20, 5)$ and $(10, 3)$. Calculate the acceleration of the object.
questions.explanation: Acceleration $a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{5-3}{20-10} = \frac{2}{10} = 0.2\text{ ms}^{-2}$.

questions.stem: A force $\vec{F} = 2i + 4j$ acts on a body and moves it through a displacement $\vec{S} = i + 5j$. Find the work done.
questions.explanation: Work done $W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{S} = (2 \times 1 + 4 \times 5) = 2 + 20 = 22\text{ J}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following units is derived?
questions.explanation: Newton (N) is a derived unit ($ ext{kg}\cdot ext{m/s}^2$), others are fundamental.

questions.stem: The slope of a straight line displacement-time graph represents?
questions.explanation: The slope ($ rac{Delta s}{Delta t}$) of a displacement-time graph gives the velocity of the object.

questions.stem: An object of mass $50\text{ kg}$ is projected with a velocity of $20\text{ ms}^{-1}$ at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ to the vertical. Calculate the time of flight.
questions.explanation: If $\theta = 60^{\circ}$ to the vertical, then $\alpha = 30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. $T = \frac{2u \sin\alpha}{g} = \frac{2(20)\sin30^{\circ}}{10} = \frac{40(0.5)}{10} = 2\text{ s}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following set of quantities is fundamental?
questions.explanation: Fundamental quantities are those that cannot be derived from other quantities. Length, mass, and time are fundamental in mechanics.

questions.stem: Given that the period of oscillation of a pendulum is given by $T = k l^x m^y g^z$ where $k$ is a constant. Find the value of $x$, $y$ and $z$.
questions.explanation: Using dimensional analysis: $[T] = [L]^x [M]^y [LT^{-2}]^z$. This results in $y=0$, $x+z=0$, and $-2z=1 \Rightarrow z=-1/2, x=1/2$.

questions.stem: A constant force $20\text{ N}$ moves a body of mass $32\text{ kg}$ with constant speed of $0.2\text{ ms}^{-1}$. Calculate the power expended.
questions.explanation: Power $P = F \cdot v$. Substituting $F = 20\text{ N}$ and $v = 0.2\text{ ms}^{-1}$, $P = 20 \times 0.2 = 4\text{ W}$.

questions.stem: If no net force acts on an object, the object maintains a state of rest or constant speed in a straight line. The above is a statement of which law?
questions.explanation: Newton's first law (Law of Inertia) states that an object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by a net external force.

questions.stem: A bullet fired vertically upwards reached a height of $500\text{ m}$. Neglecting air resistance, calculate the magnitude of the initial velocity of the bullet. ($g = 10\text{ ms}^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: Using $v^2 = u^2 - 2gh$ with final velocity $v = 0$: $u = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 500} = \sqrt{10000} = 100\text{ ms}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: A constant force of $5\text{ N}$ acts for $5\text{ s}$ on a mass of $5\text{ kg}$ initially at rest. Calculate the final momentum.
questions.explanation: Impulse = Change in momentum: $\Delta p = F \cdot t = 5\text{ N} \times 5\text{ s} = 25\text{ kg\cdot ms}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: The graph showing the variation in the angle of deviation of light through prism with the angle of incidence is?
questions.explanation: The $i-\delta$ graph for a prism is a parabolic curve with a minimum deviation point.

questions.stem: The acceleration of a moving object is equal to?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity with respect to time, which is the slope (gradient) of a velocity-time graph.

questions.stem: A chemical balance is used for measuring ……..
questions.explanation: A chemical balance measures the mass of substances by comparing it with known masses.

questions.stem: A car travelling at $30\text{ ms}^{-1}$ overcomes a frictional force of $100\text{ N}$ while moving. Calculate the power developed by the engine.
questions.explanation: Power $P = F \cdot v = 100\text{ N} \times 30\text{ ms}^{-1} = 3000\text{ W} = 3\text{ kW}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the unit of moment of inertia?
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia $I = \sum mr^2$, so the units are mass $\times$ distance squared ($ ext{kg}\cdot ext{m}^2$).

questions.stem: When an elastic material is stretched by a force, the energy stored in it is?
questions.explanation: Elastic potential energy is the energy stored as a result of applying a force to deform an elastic object.

questions.stem: A body is projected with an initial velocity $u$ at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. The time taken by it to reach its maximum height is given by?
questions.explanation: At max height, $v_y = 0$. Using $v_y = u\sin\theta - gt \Rightarrow t = u\sin\theta / g$.

questions.stem: Acceleration $a$ is calculated thus?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity: $a = \frac{v - u}{t}$.

questions.stem: A body of mass $1000\text{ kg}$ is released from a height of $10\text{ m}$ above the ground. Determine its kinetic energy just before it strikes the ground. ($g = 10\text{ ms}^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: By conservation of energy, $KE_{\text{final}} = PE_{\text{initial}} = mgh = 1000 \times 10 \times 10 = 100,000\text{ J} = 100\text{ kJ}$.

questions.stem: The mass of the Earth is $6.0 \times 10^{24}\text{ kg}$ and that of the Moon is $7.0 \times 10^{22}\text{ kg}$. If the distance between them is $4.0 \times 10^{8}\text{ m}$, calculate the force of attraction between them. ($G = 6.7 \times 10^{-11}\text{ Nm}^2/\text{kg}^2$)
questions.explanation: Gravitational force $F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2} = 6.7 \times 10^{-11} \frac{6 \times 10^{24} \times 7 \times 10^{22}}{(4 \times 10^8)^2} \approx 1.75 \times 10^{20}\text{ N}$.

questions.stem: The product $PV$, where $P$ is pressure and $V$ is the volume, has the same dimension as?
questions.explanation: Pressure $\times$ Volume = $(\text{Force}/\text{Area}) \times \text{Volume} = (\text{F}/L^2) \times L^3 = F \cdot L$, which is the dimension of Work/Energy.

questions.stem: A student measures the volume of a liquid using a measuring cylinder. What else needs to be measured in order to determine the density of the liquid?
questions.explanation: Density $\rho = \frac{m}{V}$. If volume $V$ is known, mass $m$ must be determined.

questions.stem: When a body is thrown vertically upwards, its velocity at the maximum height is?
questions.explanation: At the peak of its trajectory, the body momentarily stops before changing direction, so its velocity is zero.

questions.stem: Material that can be stretched and still return to the original form when the stresses are removed are said to be …
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the property of a material to return to its original shape after deformation.

questions.stem: When the linear momentum of a body is constant, the net force acting on it is?
questions.explanation: By Newton's 2nd Law, $F = \frac{dp}{dt}$. If $p$ is constant, $\frac{dp}{dt} = 0$.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities is made up of vectors?
questions.explanation: Displacement and acceleration both have magnitude and specific direction.

questions.stem: The S.I. unit of power is…..
questions.explanation: The SI unit of power is the Watt (W), which is 1 Joule per second.

questions.stem: A simple pendulum makes 50 oscillations in one minute. Determine its period of oscillation.
questions.explanation: Period $T = \frac{\text{Total Time}}{\text{Number of oscillations}} = \frac{60\text{ s}}{50} = 1.2\text{ s}$.

questions.stem: A car starts from rest and covers a distance of $40\text{ m}$ in $10\text{ s}$. Calculate the magnitude of its acceleration.
questions.explanation: Using $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$: $40 = 0(10) + \frac{1}{2}a(10)^2 \Rightarrow 40 = 50a \Rightarrow a = 0.8\text{ ms}^{-2}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following unit is equivalent to Watt?
questions.explanation: $1\text{ W} = 1\text{ J/s} = (1\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-2})/\text{s} = \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-3}$.

questions.stem: The acceleration of a moving particle is given as $a(t) = (-3 + t^2)\text{ ms}^{-2}$. Find its velocity at time $t = 3\text{ s}$, given that the velocity at $t = 0$ is zero.
Which of the following devices is used to determine the relative density of an acid?
questions.explanation: A hydrometer is used to measure the specific gravity (relative density) of liquids.

questions.stem: The electricity meters in houses measure energy units consumed in……
questions.explanation: Domestic electricity is billed based on energy, typically measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).

questions.stem: The tendency of a stationary body to continue to remain at rest when a force is applied to it is known as?
questions.explanation: Inertia is the inherent resistance of any physical object to any change in its state of motion.

questions.stem: The total area under a force-velocity graph represents?
questions.explanation: Power is defined as $F \cdot v$. The integral of power over time is energy, but the instantaneous product is power.

questions.stem: The sound heard by a person after the reflection of the sound generated by him is called?
questions.explanation: An echo is a reflection of sound that arrives at the listener with a delay after the direct sound.

questions.stem: Which of the following dimensions represents impulse?
questions.explanation: Impulse = Force $\times$ Time = $(MLT^{-2}) \times T = MLT^{-1}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an example of kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: All the options involve motion, and therefore all are examples of kinetic energy.

questions.stem: Identify the correct dimensions of density and pressure from the following:
questions.explanation: Density = Mass/Volume = $M/L^3 = ML^{-3}$. Pressure = Force/Area = $(MLT^{-2})/L^2 = ML^{-1}T^{-2}$.

questions.stem: The energy stored in a spring of stiffness constant $k = 2000\text{ Nm}^{-1}$ when extended by $4\text{ cm}$ is …

A bullet of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ is fired with a velocity of $800\text{ ms}^{-1}$ into a soft wood of mass $2\text{ kg}$, lying on a smooth surface. What is the final velocity if the collision is completely inelastic?
questions.explanation: Conservation of momentum: $m_1 u_1 = (m_1 + m_2)v \Rightarrow 0.2 \times 800 = (2.2)v \Rightarrow 160 = 2.2v \Rightarrow v \approx 72.7\text{ ms}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: Range of a projected particle can be expressed as?
questions.explanation: Range is horizontal distance: $R = v_x \times T_{\text{total}} = (u \cos\theta) \times T$.

questions.stem: A boy of mass $60\text{ kg}$ runs up a set of steps of total height $3\text{ m}$. Work done in joules is ___ (take $g = 10\text{ ms}^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: Work done against gravity $W = mgh = 60 \times 10 \times 3 = 1800\text{ J}$.

questions.stem: The maximum force that must be overcome before a body starts to move is called?
questions.explanation: Static friction is the friction that exists between a stationary object and the surface on which it's resting.

questions.stem: The density of a block is $150\text{ g}\cdot\text{cm}^{-3}$ and has a mass of $80\text{ g}$. Calculate the volume of the block.
questions.explanation: $V = \frac{m}{\rho} = \frac{80}{150} \approx 0.533\text{ cm}^3$.

questions.stem: Which of the following readings cannot be determined with a micrometer screw gauge?
questions.explanation: A standard micrometer has a range of about $2.5\text{ cm}$ ($25\text{ mm}$); $21\text{ cm}$ is way outside its physical capacity.

questions.stem: A man of mass $50\text{ kg}$ ascends a flight of stairs $5\text{ m}$ high in $5\text{ seconds}$. If acceleration due to gravity is $10\text{ ms}^{-2}$, the power expended is……
questions.explanation: Power $P = \frac{mgh}{t} = \frac{50 \times 10 \times 5}{5} = 500\text{ W}$.

questions.stem: Under which of the following conditions is work done?

options.A: A man supports a heavy load above his head with his hands
options.B: A boy climbs onto a table
options.D: A bag of cocoa stands on a platform

questions.explanation: Work is done only when a force results in displacement. Climbing involves vertical displacement.

questions.stem: A loaded test-tube which floats upright in water is carefully and slightly depressed and then released. Which of the following best describes the subsequent motion of the test tube?
questions.explanation: The restoring force (upthrust) causes the tube to move back and forth through its equilibrium position.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: This is the first equation of linear motion for constant acceleration.

questions.stem: Physics is a pure science that deals with?

options.C: Relationship between different forms of energy

questions.explanation: The fundamental definition of Physics is the study of matter, energy, and the interactions between them.

questions.stem: A car travelling at a uniform speed of $120\text{ km/h}$ passes two stations in $4\text{ minutes}$. Calculate the distance between the two stations.
questions.explanation: Distance $d = v \times t = 120\text{ km/h} \times (4/60)\text{ h} = 120 \times \frac{1}{15} = 8\text{ km}$.

questions.stem: The branch of physics that deals with sound and waves is?
questions.explanation: Acoustics is the interdisciplinary science that deals with the study of mechanical waves in gases, liquids, and solids.

questions.stem: Which of the units of the following physical quantities is not a derived unit?
questions.explanation: Mass is a base (fundamental) quantity in the SI system.

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect?
questions.explanation: Speed is a scalar quantity because it does not have a specified direction.

questions.stem: Which of these motions could be uniform?
questions.explanation: Uniform circular motion describes motion in a circle at a constant speed.

questions.stem: What is the engine power of a car with retarding force $500\text{ N}$ moving at constant speed $20\text{ ms}^{-1}$?
questions.explanation: $P = F \times v = 500 \times 20 = 10,000\text{ W} = 10\text{ kW}$.

questions.stem: The speed of a bullet of mass $20\text{ g}$ is $216\text{ km/h}$. What is its kinetic energy in joules?
The main cause of motion is?
questions.explanation: According to Newton's laws, a force is required to change the state of motion of an object.

questions.stem: A ball of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ moving at $10\text{ ms}^{-1}$ collides with another ball of equal mass at rest. If the two balls move together after impact, calculate their common velocity.
questions.explanation: $m_1 u_1 = (m_1 + m_2)v \Rightarrow 0.5(10) = (1.0)v \Rightarrow v = 5\text{ ms}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly gives the relationship between linear speed $v$ and angular speed $\omega$ of a body moving uniformly in a circle of radius $r$?
questions.explanation: Linear velocity is the product of the angular velocity and the radius of the circular path.

questions.stem: The motion of a body is simple harmonic if the?

options.A: Acceleration is always directed towards a fixed point
options.B: Path of motion is a straight line
options.C: Acceleration is directed towards a fixed point and proportional to its distance from the point
options.D: Acceleration is constant and directed towards a fixed point

questions.explanation: This is the defining condition for SHM: $a \propto -x$.

questions.stem: What is the angular speed of a body vibrating at $50\text{ cycles per second}$?
questions.explanation: $\omega = 2\pi f = 2 \times 3.142 \times 50 \approx 314.2\text{ rad/s}$.

questions.stem: When a mass attached to a spiral spring is set into vertical oscillations, its acceleration will have a?

options.A: Varying magnitude but a constant direction
options.B: Constant magnitude and a constant direction
options.C: Constant magnitude but a varying direction
options.D: Varying magnitude and a varying direction

questions.explanation: In SHM, acceleration changes magnitude based on displacement and changes direction as it passes the equilibrium point.

questions.stem: For a simple pendulum of length $l$, the period is given by?
questions.explanation: The standard formula for the period of a simple pendulum for small angles.

questions.stem: Which is the incorrect formula for a body accelerating uniformly?
questions.explanation: The correct formula is $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$.

questions.stem: A catapult is used to project a stone. Which of the following energy conversions takes place as the stone is released?

options.A: Kinetic energy is converted into potential energy
options.B: Gravitational potential energy is converted into kinetic energy
options.C: Elastic potential energy is converted into kinetic energy
options.D: Gravitational potential energy is converted into elastic potential energy

questions.explanation: The stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy, which transfers to the stone as kinetic energy.

questions.stem: For a freely falling body:

options.A: The ratio of kinetic energy to potential energy is constant
options.B: The sum of kinetic and potential energies is constant
options.C: The total energy is entirely kinetic
options.D: The total energy is entirely potential

questions.explanation: According to the law of conservation of mechanical energy, $TME = KE + PE$ stays constant.

questions.stem: A stationary ball is hit by an average force of $50\text{ N}$ for a time of $0.03\text{ s}$. What is the impulse experienced by the body in $\text{N}\cdot\text{s}$?
questions.explanation: Impulse $I = F \times t = 50 \times 0.03 = 1.5\text{ N}\cdot\text{s}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an example of force?
questions.explanation: Mass is a scalar quantity representing the amount of matter; the others are types of forces (vectors).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Glass is an insulator because it does not have free electrons to carry charge.

questions.stem: Power is defined as the?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate at which work is performed or energy is converted.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of motion does a body undergo when moving in a haphazard manner?
questions.explanation: Random motion (like Brownian motion) lacks a predictable path.

questions.stem: Which of the following quantities has the same unit as energy?
questions.explanation: Both Work and Energy are measured in Joules (J).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Distance has only magnitude, whereas tension, impulse, and force have both magnitude and direction.

questions.stem: Two bodies each carrying a charge of $2.00 \times 10^{-10}\text{ C}$ are $5\text{ cm}$ apart. Calculate the magnitude of the force on the charges. ($1/4\pi\epsilon_0 = 9 \times 10^9\text{ Nm}^2\text{C}^{-2}$)
Which of the following sources of energy is renewable?
questions.explanation: Hydro energy relies on the water cycle, which is naturally replenished.

questions.stem: If an object of mass $50\text{ kg}$ moves at $5\text{ ms}^{-1}$ round a circular path of radius $10\text{ m}$, calculate the centripetal force needed to keep it in its orbit.
questions.explanation: $F_c = \frac{mv^2}{r} = \frac{50 \times 5^2}{10} = \frac{50 \times 25}{10} = 125\text{ N}$.

questions.stem: A boy of mass $20\text{ kg}$ moves at $5\text{ ms}^{-1}$ round a circular path of radius $10\text{ m}$, calculate the centripetal acceleration.
The type of collision in which the two objects join together after an impact and move with the same velocity is termed?
questions.explanation: In a perfectly inelastic collision, the maximum amount of kinetic energy is lost and the bodies stick together.

questions.stem: Given $T^2 = 4\pi^2 \cdot L/g$, which of the following is the correct equation for $g$ if a graph of $T^2$ is plotted against $L$?
questions.explanation: Slope $S = T^2 / L = 4\pi^2 / g \Rightarrow g = 4\pi^2 / S$.

questions.stem: The period of oscillation of a simple pendulum is related to its length $L$ and acceleration $g$ by $T = K L^x g^y$. Determine $x$ and $y$ where $K$ is a constant.
Given that the period of oscillation of a pendulum is $T = k L^x g^y m^z$, find the values of $x$, $y$, and $z$ where $k$ is a constant.
questions.explanation: The period is independent of mass, so $z=0$. $x=1/2$ and $y=-1/2$.

questions.stem: A chemical balance is used for measuring?
questions.explanation: A chemical balance measures mass, unlike a spring balance which measures weight.

questions.stem: Material that can be stretched and still return to the original forms when the stresses are removed are said to be?
questions.explanation: Definition of elasticity.

questions.stem: A simple pendulum makes $X$ oscillations in one minute. Determine $X$ if its period of oscillation is $1.20\text{ s}$.
Which of the following is the unit of force?
questions.explanation: The Newton (N) is the SI unit of force.

questions.stem: Which of the following graphs will give us more information?
questions.explanation: Non-linear graphs can describe complex physical relationships that straight lines cannot.

questions.stem: What type of relationship exists between $A$ and $B$ if the increase in value of $A$ brings a decrease in value of $B$?
questions.explanation: In an inverse relationship, variables move in opposite directions.

questions.stem: The dependent variable in the equation $F = ke$ is?
questions.explanation: Usually, $F$ is measured as a response to changes in $e$ (extension).

questions.stem: The point where the line of best fit touches the vertical axis is called?
questions.explanation: The vertical intercept (y-intercept).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an essential component of a graph?
questions.explanation: All listed are essential for a complete scientific graph.

questions.stem: The slope of the graph obtained in a simple pendulum experiment when a graph of $l$ is plotted against $T^2$ is $0.25\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Determine the value of $g$.
questions.explanation: $S = l/T^2 = g/(4\pi^2) \Rightarrow g = S \cdot 4\pi^2 = 0.25 \times 4 \times 9.87 \approx 9.87\text{ ms}^{-2}$.

questions.stem: In a simple pendulum experiment, the value of $T$ _________ as the value of $l$ increases.
questions.explanation: $T \propto \sqrt{l}$.

questions.stem: The period of oscillation of a simple pendulum is $2\text{ s}$ when the length of the string is $64\text{ cm}$. Calculate the period if the string’s length is shortened to $49\text{ cm}$.
A force of $10\text{ N}$ produced an extension of $2.50\text{ cm}$. Determine the spring constant.
In Hooke’s law experiment, a graph of the extension $e$ was plotted against Force $F$. If the slope of the graph is $0.4\text{ mN}^{-1}$, what is the value of $k$?
questions.explanation: $S = e/F = 1/k \Rightarrow k = 1/S = 1/0.4 = 2.5\text{ N/m}$.

questions.stem: The energy stored in a spring of stiffness constant $k = 2000\text{ N/m}$ when extended by $4\text{ cm}$ is?
Which of the following affect the period of a simple pendulum?
questions.explanation: Period depends only on $l$ and $g$ for small amplitudes.

questions.stem: The frequency of a certain pendulum A is $10\text{ cycles per second}$, and the frequency of another pendulum B is $5\text{ cycles per second}$. Which pendulum is longer in length?

options.D: A is slightly longer than B

questions.explanation: $f = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{g/l}$, so frequency is inversely proportional to square root of length. Lower frequency means longer length.

questions.stem: The period of Oscillation can be defined as?
questions.explanation: Definition of period.

questions.stem: The main reading of a Vernier calliper is $6.2\text{ cm}$. If the main scale and the vernier scale coincides at the $7^{th}$ position, what is the total reading of the instrument?
questions.explanation: Reading = $6.2 + (7 \times 0.01) = 6.27\text{ cm}$.

questions.stem: The diameter of a piece of wire can be measured most accurately with a?
questions.explanation: Micrometers have higher precision (usually 0.01 mm) compared to calipers (0.1 mm).

questions.stem: Which of the following represent the correct precision if the length of a piece of wire is measured with a metre rule?
questions.explanation: A meter rule has a least count of 1 mm (0.1 cm), so the reading should reflect that precision.

questions.stem: The smallest scale division of a Vernier caliper is?
questions.explanation: The least count of a standard Vernier caliper.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a part of the micrometer screw gauge?
questions.explanation: Anvil, spindle, and thimble are all essential parts of a micrometer.

questions.stem: The clenched jaws of the anvil and the spindle are brought into contact through?
questions.explanation: The ratchet stop prevents over-tightening and ensures uniform pressure.

questions.stem: A simple pendulum $0.64\text{ m}$ long has a period of $1.2\text{ s}$. Calculate the period of a similar pendulum $0.36\text{ m}$ long in the same location.
An error due to inherent defects in the method or apparatus used is called?
questions.explanation: Systematic errors are predictable and typically constant or proportional to the true value.

questions.stem: Errors due to personal peculiarities of an observer where human reaction or estimation affects the results are called?
questions.explanation: Errors caused by human limitations, such as parallax or slow reaction time.

questions.stem: The only way to eliminate systematic errors is to…
questions.explanation: Since they are built-in, only correction or calibration of the device can remove them.

questions.stem: The only remedy to random errors is to…
questions.explanation: Averaging multiple readings tends to cancel out positive and negative random fluctuations.

questions.stem: Errors due to the accuracy of the division of graduated scales on the instrument is called?
questions.explanation: A specific type of systematic error caused by poor manufacturing of the instrument.

questions.stem: Errors due to unknown causes or chance are known as?
questions.explanation: Definition of random errors.

questions.stem: Experimental errors are usually divided into two main types which are?
questions.explanation: The two broadest categories in error analysis.

questions.stem: At a glance, _____ gives a comprehensive picture of the experiment than the data themselves.
questions.explanation: Graphs provide a visual representation of trends and relationships.

questions.stem: The general form of the equation which yields a straight line is?
questions.explanation: The standard linear equation.

questions.stem: The S.I. unit of spring constant is?
questions.explanation: $k = F/x$, so Newtons per meter.

questions.stem: To get the elongation $e$ in Hooke’s experiment of elasticity, where $L_1$ is the initial length and $L_2$ is the new length, the equation is?
questions.explanation: Extension is the change in length.

questions.stem: The change in velocity of a body at a particular time is known as?
questions.explanation: The derivative of velocity with respect to time.

questions.stem: If two vectors are represented thus: $\vec{A} = 5i + 2j + k$ and $\vec{B} = 2i + 4j - 3k$. Find $\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B}$.
questions.explanation: $\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = (5 \times 2) + (2 \times 4) + (1 \times -3) = 10 + 8 - 3 = 15$.

questions.stem: An object of mass $50\text{ kg}$ is projected with a velocity of $20\text{ ms}^{-1}$ at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. Calculate the time of flight.
_____ is defined as the process used to check the validity of a specific equation in mechanics.
questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis ensures both sides of an equation have identical units.

questions.stem: The independent variable in the equation $F = ke$ is ….
questions.explanation: The extension is controlled/changed by the experimenter to see the response in force.
